Wiktor Tomasik — Strange loop in J-space

What a language model builds when a description of itself is looped back into itself.
Research presented in The Mind in the Mirror: Self-Models at https://pixedar.github.io/.

Four experiments study reflective feedback, a learning self-model's surprise, a frozen decision-position loop, and a trained loop across reasoning segments. J-space is the initial candidate bottleneck for reading internal states as words; the later loop learns a compact state. Loops preserve what they can regenerate, not necessarily what is their own. Current surprise can drive exploration without privileged self-knowledge. Self-specificity requires private state in these experiments.

In the trained Qwen3-8B and Qwen3-14B loops, discriminative self-prediction pressure produces a multi-frequency clock of reasoning stages when the self-model must distinguish its own moments, or a persistent identity code when it must distinguish traces. Feeding back a self-forecast causes the next state to move toward it. Strong pressure sacrifices content; mild pressure preserves both content and enactment.

All measures are functional and do not establish experience. Training uses fixed traces, seed replication is limited, and free generation loses the topic. Corrections include resemblance rather than ownership, precision-limited near-fixed points, collapse behind early self-prediction scores, and a robust rotation fit rather than a consistently coherent single clock plane. Own-state reliance differs from benefit over a constant input. The full report records the controls and corrections.

Author: Wiktor Tomasik
Code and full report: https://github.com/Pixedar/jspace-strange-loop
Data: https://huggingface.co/datasets/Pixedar/jspace-strange-loop
Earlier writing: https://medium.com/@pixedar
